months.title: October 2026
months.summary: A lens month, and finally a big one for Nikon. Nikon released the NIKKOR Z 120-300mm f/2.8 TC VR S, the first constant f/2.8 telephoto zoom with a built-in 1.4x teleconverter, aimed squarely at sports. Third-party makers kept filling out Z mount: Tamron brought its 20-40mm f/2.8 and a new 16-50mm f/2.8 APS-C zoom, Viltrox finished its f/1.4 Pro trio with a 35mm, and Sigma ported its 16-300mm superzoom. Sigma also announced the fp2, a tiny full-frame L-mount camera with a partially stacked sensor and 6K open gate, plus a compact 50-120mm f/2.8 for APS-C and an all-metal 50mm f/1.4 CL. Sony, Canon and Panasonic were quiet, and Fujifilm raised its prices in Japan instead of launching anything.
months.forYou: The 120-300mm f/2.8 TC is the one to watch for sports on your Z7 II: it covers your Sigma 70-200 and goes to 420mm, but at $13,997 it's a rental for most jobs. The Viltrox 35mm f/1.4 Pro ($829) and Tamron 20-40mm f/2.8 are native Z lenses that would fill the wide gap below your 24-70 without the FTZ.

months.title: September 2026
months.summary: A big month for telephoto lenses and a quiet one for Nikon. Sony shrank the super-telephoto with a sub-1 kg 400mm f/4.5 and 600mm f/6.3, and added its first full-frame fisheye zoom. Canon finally put IBIS in its cheapest full-frame body with the EOS R8 Mark II. Fujifilm gave X shooters a 400mm f/4.5 prime, and Sigma filled out its E and L lineups with an 85mm f/1.2 and a wide 20-60mm walkaround zoom. OM System revived the PEN name. Nikon only announced products in development: nine cinema lenses built with RED, and firmware 2.0 for the ZR.
months.forYou: Nothing new for your Z7 II this month. Nikon's announcements are development notices only, and the new Sigma lenses are E and L mount.
